description:
Team Protocol Ares is taking on the Space Mission Design Game challenge. We believe the best way to understand space exploration is to try running a mission yourself.

Our game, Selenares (from Selene, goddess of the Moon, and Ares, god of Mars), puts students and young people in command of a four-person base on the Moon or Mars. Each day, players divide limited crew hours between life support, greenhouse farming, solar power, radiation shielding, medical care and research.
summary:
Selenares is a free browser game where players command a four-person survival base on the Moon or Mars. Each day, they split limited crew hours between life support, greenhouse farming, solar power, radiation shielding, medical care and research, and must keep the crew alive until the resupply ship arrives. Every system affects the others: farms and air scrubbers need energy, radiation wears down health, and low morale cuts output.

The game teaches real space science through play. Events such as solar flares, dust storms, micrometeorites and a Mars communications blackout force tough choices, each with a “Did you know?” fact. A Mission Control quiz appears every four days. A built-in Codex compares Earth, the Moon and Mars on gravity, radiation, temperature, air and radio delay.

Players unlock 12 upgrades, manage crew with different roles, complete mission goals and watch their base grow on screen. Missions run 10, 20 or 30 days at three difficulty levels. The game runs in any browser, including on phones, with no installation.
details:
Our game, Selenares (from Selene, goddess of the Moon, and Ares, god of Mars), puts students and young people in command of a four-person base on the Moon or Mars. Each day, players divide limited crew hours between life support, greenhouse farming, solar power, radiation shielding, medical care and research. Every system depends on the others, so they must make trade-offs just like real mission planners.

Selenares teaches through play:

  • Players survive 10, 20 or 30 days at three difficulty levels, facing events such as solar flares, dust storms, micrometeorites and a Mars communications blackout.
  • Each event includes a “Did you know?” fact, and a Mission Control quiz every four days rewards correct answers.
  • A built-in Codex compares Earth, the Moon and Mars on gravity, radiation, temperature, air and radio delay.
  • Players unlock 12 upgrades, such as hydroponics, radiation vests and a magnetic shield. They also manage a crew with different roles and complete mission goals, and the base visibly grows in the scene as they do.
  • The game includes a mini-game, rover expeditions, achievements, a Hall of Fame and save-and-resume.

Selenares runs in any browser, including on phones, as a single HTML file with no installation. Its music and sound effects are original and generated in the browser.
